newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet body clears chemical sector plan.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet body clears chemical sector plan.

text.p: The Polish government's economic council (KERM) on Monday approved a development programme for the chemical sector which provides for investing $3 billion in the largely state-owned industry over the next eight years.
Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said after the KERM meeting that half of the sum should come from foreign investors while the rest from the sector's own resources and from domestic banks.
"Poland's economy badly needs the development of this industry...We produce some 25 kg of plastics per head while the ratio is 110 kg in the United States," Kaczmarek told a news briefing.

He said the programme, named the Great Chemical Synthesis, mapped out 105 investment projects needed in the sector. The plan includes greenfield investments as well as modernisations and capacity expansion.
The government will offer guarantees for selected projects, he said.
Kaczmarek also said that although the scheme envisaged attracting foreign investors, who would be offered new shares of selected chemical firms, it would not be easy to find buyers.

The chemical companies had highly diversified production and investors were mainly interested in acquiring only the best chunks of them and not the whole firms as the government wanted, Kaczmarek said.
He said that under the programme, which will need approval by the whole cabinet, some chemical companies would be consolidated to help them survive Western competition.
But the plan would make sure that the consolidation would not lead to creating monopolies, he added.
